Make a household communication plan
Choose emergency contacts and meeting places. Keep a copy of the contact plan where your household can find it.
Review routes and places to go
Learn and practice your evacuation routes and shelter plan in advance. Follow official instructions during an emergency; this checklist does not identify safe routes or open shelters.
Gather and review emergency supplies
Use the official kit guide to plan food, water, lighting and other supplies for your household. Review the kit regularly.
Discuss household care and support
Agree with trusted people on who can help with household care, communication and supplies. Include caregivers in the plan when appropriate.
Plan accessible communication and practical assistance
Create a support network and discuss help with communication, mobility and assistive devices before an emergency.
Discuss backup arrangements for powered equipment
Discuss power-loss planning for medical or assistive equipment with your care team or equipment provider. Use their guidance for your equipment.
Arrange transportation support in advance
Discuss transportation and accessibility requirements with your support network. Confirm arrangements directly; this guide cannot book transport.
Include pets and service animals in your plan
Plan supplies, transport and a place that can accommodate your animals. Confirm arrangements directly before relying on them.
